media.title: 5,000 Steps a Day May Help Slow Alzheimer’s Changes in the Brain

timecodes.what: HealthDay medical news report on the Mass General Brigham / Harvard Aging Brain Study Nature Medicine finding that 3,000–5,000 and 5,000–7,500 daily steps slow Alzheimer's decline.
Visual summary of how daily step counts brake tau protein tangle buildup and delay cognitive decline by 3 to 7 years in amyloid-positive older adults.

media.title: Physical activity slows tau accumulation in preclinical Alzheimer's disease

timecodes.what: Walkthrough of the 296-participant Harvard Aging Brain Study design comparing baseline waist pedometers against longitudinal amyloid and tau PET imaging.
Dose-response curve showing cognitive preservation plateauing past 7,500 daily steps.
